schema_query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

columns.name: judge_name
columns.definition: The full name of the federal judge presiding over the case or issuing the order.
columns.rationale: Essential for identifying the specific judge to analyze their individual voting patterns and decisions.

columns.name: appointing_president
columns.definition: The U.S. President who appointed the federal judge to their position.
columns.rationale: Directly addresses the core query comparing Trump-appointed judges with those appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents.

columns.name: case_type
columns.definition: The specific type of immigration policy or program being challenged in the case.
columns.rationale: Helps categorize the cases to see if voting tendencies differ based on the specific immigration policy at issue (e.g., Alien Enemies Act, sponsor vetting, legal orientation programs).

columns.name: ruling_on_injunction
columns.definition: The court's decision regarding the requested preliminary injunction or temporary restraining order.
columns.rationale: Directly measures the judge's voting tendency and supportiveness toward the challenged administration policy.
allowed_values: Granted in part, Denied in part

columns.name: supportive_of_administration_policy
columns.definition: Indicates whether the judge's ruling ultimately upheld or supported the executive branch's immigration policy or action.
columns.rationale: Directly answers the research question regarding whether judges are supportive of the administration's policies.
